metaDescription: Six miter saws at or under $300 from DEWALT, SKIL and Evolution, from 7-1/4 inch compact to 12 inch and cordless, compared on capacity, bevel and fence height.
expertTake: The DEWALT DWS713 is the pick for most workshops because a 15 amp motor, 14 positive stops and a tall sliding fence deliver the cut accuracy trim carpenters need at a price that still fits this cap. The SKIL MS6305 is the value pick if you need to cut wide boards, since a sliding arm and dual bevel arrive for the cost of many fixed saws. Skip a 7-1/4 inch compact saw if you cut 2x6 or crown regularly, because the blade diameter, not the motor, sets the width the saw can cross-cut. The extra budget over an entry saw mostly buys stiffer castings, steadier detents and a taller fence.
introParagraphs: A miter saw swings a blade down onto a board held against a fence, which gives repeatable crosscuts and angles that no handheld saw can match. The three specs that decide a saw's usefulness are blade diameter, whether the head slides, and how tall the fence is, and the box rarely explains the interaction among them.

This guide explains what the upper end of a modest budget buys in a miter saw, how crosscut width and fence height limit the work, and why motor amps matter less than detent accuracy. The picks are listed above, with the reviews below. Listing prices move, and the cap reflects prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: DEWALT DWS713 10 Inch Single Bevel Compound Miter Saw, 15 Amp
products.description:
A stainless-steel miter detent plate with 14 positive stops is the heart of this saw's accuracy. Positive stops are notches that click the saw to common angles like 22.5 and 45 degrees, and stainless resists the wear that rounds off softer plates. A machined base fence support keeps the fence square to the blade, and a tall sliding fence supports a 4-1/4 inch base molding standing vertically.

The saw is a 10 inch fixed-head design, so it crosscuts about 6 inches in a single pass, narrower than the SKIL MS6305's sliding arm. In exchange you get a simpler, stiffer machine with fewer parts to wear. Compared with the 12 inch DEWALT DWS715, the DWS713 is lighter and less expensive, but the DWS715 handles taller base molding. For trim, baseboard and window casing, 10 inches is the sweet spot.

Ownership: set the fence square and check the detent plate before the first cut, because a saw that is off by half a degree ruins miters. Replace the stock blade with an 80-tooth finish blade for trim. Clean sawdust from the pivot and plate regularly, and use a vacuum on the dust port, since the onboard bag catches only part of the dust.
products.bestFor: Trim carpenters and DIYers who want a precise 10 inch fixed saw with a tall fence.
pros: Stainless detent plate with 14 stops stays accurate over years
15 amp motor cuts hardwood trim without bogging
Tall fence supports 4-1/4 inch base molding vertically
Fixed head is stiff and simple to adjust
cons: Crosscut width is limited to about 6 inches without a slide
Single bevel requires flipping the board for opposite angles
Dust collection is partial with the onboard bag

products.name: DEWALT DWS715 12 Inch Single Bevel Compound Miter Saw, 15 Amp
products.description:
The jump from a 10 inch blade to a 12 inch blade raises crosscut capacity and cut depth, which lets this saw handle 5-1/2 inch base molding standing vertically against the fence. It shares the stainless detent plate and 14 stops of the DWS713, so angle accuracy is the same, and the same 15 amp motor spins the larger blade.

The tradeoff is size and cost. A 12 inch saw is bigger, heavier and costlier than the DWS713, and the larger blade costs more to replace. Against the SKIL MS6305, the DEWALT cuts a thicker board in one pass, but the SKIL slides to cut wider boards. If you work on tall crown, thick posts or wide trim, the 12 inch blade is worth it.

Ownership: a 12 inch blade is heavier, so check the arbor and the blade guard condition. Use a thin-kerf blade to reduce motor load, and clean the detent plate. The saw is heavy, so a stable stand or a bench with clamps keeps it from walking during cuts.
products.bestFor: Remodelers who cut tall base molding and thick stock and want a 12 inch blade.
pros: 12 inch blade cuts thicker stock and taller molding
Stainless detent plate with 14 stops
15 amp motor drives the larger blade well
Fence supports 5-1/2 inch base molding vertically
cons: Larger and heavier than 10 inch saws
Highest relative price in the roundup

products.name: SKIL MS6305-00 10 Inch Dual Bevel Sliding Compound Miter Saw

specList.label: Bevel
specList.value: Dual bevel, 48 and 45 degrees left, 45 right

products.description:
A sliding head carries the blade along rails so it can cut boards wider than the blade radius, and a dual bevel tilts both left and right so you never flip the board for opposite angles. This SKIL pairs the two with a 15 amp motor at 4,800 RPM, which is the combination that usually costs far more. An LED shadow line projects the blade's edge onto the wood, which is more precise than a laser dot because it shows the actual kerf.

The tradeoff is accuracy over the long term. Sliding rails add play that a fixed head does not have, so a budget slider needs more setup to stay square than the DEWALT DWS713. Compared with the DWS713, the SKIL crosscuts wider boards and bevels both ways, but the DEWALT holds angles better. For a shop that cuts shelving and 1x12 boards, the slide is the feature you pay for.

Ownership: check that the fence is square to the blade, and tighten the rail bearings if the head wobbles. Use the stock blade for rough cuts and swap in a fine blade for trim. Wipe the rails and keep them free of dust. The LED shadow line needs the light bulb to be clean.
products.bestFor: DIYers who cut wide shelving and want a sliding dual bevel saw at a low relative price.
pros: Sliding head crosscuts boards wider than a fixed 10 inch saw
Dual bevel eliminates flipping boards for opposite angles
LED shadow line shows the true kerf
15 amp motor at 4,800 RPM cuts cleanly
cons: Slide rails add play and need setup to stay square
Heavier and bulkier than fixed saws
Detent accuracy is less proven than the DEWALT plate

products.name: DEWALT DCS714B 20V MAX XR 10 Inch Double Bevel Fixed Miter Saw (Tool Only)

specList.label: Runtime claim
specList.value: Up to 434 cuts in 3-1/4 inch MDF base

products.description:
A bevel gear transmission turns the motor's output into blade rotation with less loss than a belt, which is how a battery-powered saw reaches usable runtime. The listing claims up to 434 cuts in 3-1/4 inch MDF base molding, a figure that depends on battery size. It is described as the first 10 inch DEWALT miter saw that works with the full range of 20V MAX and FLEXVOLT batteries.

The tradeoff is the bare tool: no battery, no charger, so it makes sense only if you already own the platform. Against the corded DWS713, the cordless saw frees you from an outlet and extension cord on job sites, but a big pack adds cost. A fixed head crosscuts a narrower board than the sliding SKIL. For trim crews who move between rooms, going cordless is a real time saver.

Ownership: use a larger pack for long sessions, and charge before each day. Keep the blade sharp, since a dull blade drains a battery faster than anything else. Check the dust port and clean the pivot, and store batteries away from heat.
products.bestFor: Trim crews who own 20V MAX or FLEXVOLT batteries and want a cordless 10 inch saw.
pros: Cordless freedom on job sites without extension cords
Double bevel avoids flipping boards
Bevel gear transmission improves efficiency
Works with 20V MAX and FLEXVOLT batteries
cons: Tool only, so batteries and a charger cost extra
Runtime depends heavily on pack size

products.name: Evolution R185SMS+ Sliding Miter Saw, 210mm Multi-Material Blade
products.description:
A multi-material blade with carbide teeth cuts steel, aluminum and wood on the same saw, which is the point of this machine. Dry metal cutting produces fewer sparks than an abrasive chop saw, and the listing says it leaves an instantly usable edge. A 15 amp motor with a high-torque gearbox drives the 210 millimeter blade, which is about 8-1/4 inches.

The tradeoff is that this is a different kind of saw. A smaller blade limits crosscut width and depth compared with the 10 inch DEWALT, and it is not a finish saw for fine trim. Versus the SKIL MS6305, the Evolution cuts metal that the SKIL cannot, but gives up wood-cutting finish quality. For a shop that cuts conduit, angle iron and framing in one job, the versatility is the sell.

Ownership: wear eye and hearing protection, since metal cutting is loud. Metal chips accumulate, so clean them out of the base. Use the right blade for each material and replace it when teeth dull. Never cut hot-rolled steel with a wood blade.
products.bestFor: Fabricators and remodelers who cut metal conduit, angle and wood on one saw.
pros: Multi-material blade cuts steel, aluminum and wood
Dry cutting leaves a usable edge with fewer sparks
15 amp high-torque gearbox handles metal
Sliding head extends crosscut width
cons: Smaller 8-1/4 inch blade limits depth and width
Finish quality in wood trails dedicated wood blades
Metal cutting is loud and throws chips

products.name: SKIL 7-1/4 Inch 10 Amp Single Bevel Miter Saw with Compact Rail System

specList.label: Mount
specList.value: Compact fixed rail, stand sold separately

products.description:
A fixed compact rail system lets the saw's arm slide while keeping its footprint small against a wall. The listing claims a crosscut of up to 2x10 at 0 degrees and 2x6 at 45 degrees, plus 3-1/2 inch nested crown, which is wider than a fixed 7-1/4 inch saw usually cuts. An LED shadow line replaces a laser and shows the kerf.

The tradeoff is power and blade size. A 10 amp motor driving a 7-1/4 inch blade is lighter than the 15 amp saws, and thin-kerf blades are the right choice. Against the DEWALT DWS713, the SKIL is smaller and more portable, but it gives up fence height and stops. The stand is sold separately, so budget for a bench.

Ownership: because the blade is small, use a good thin-kerf blade to lighten the load. Check the rail for play and keep it clean, and clamp the saw to a bench for stability. It suits garage trim projects.
products.bestFor: Apartment and garage DIYers who need a compact saw for trim and small projects.
pros: Compact rail system saves bench and wall space
Crosscuts up to 2x10 at 0 degrees
LED shadow line shows the true kerf
Light and easy to carry
cons: 10 amp motor is the weakest in the lineup
Fence is lower than the DEWALT saws

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 10 inch blade cross-cuts about 6 inches fixed, and a 12 inch blade cuts about 8. The DEWALT DWS715 handles 5-1/2 inch base vertically, and the DWS713 handles 4-1/4. A 7-1/4 inch saw like the SKIL rail model needs its slide to reach 2x10. Pick the blade size from the widest board you cut, not from the motor.

A slide extends crosscut width, at the cost of rail play. The SKIL MS6305 slides, while the DEWALT saws are fixed. A fixed head is stiffer and holds angles better. If you cut 1x12 shelving, you need the slide. A slide also needs about a foot of clearance behind the saw, so measure your bench depth first.

A single bevel tilts one way, so opposite angles mean flipping the board. A dual bevel tilts both ways. The SKIL MS6305 and DEWALT DCS714B are dual bevel. Flipping boards wastes time on long trim runs.

Positive stops click to common angles, and a stainless plate resists wear. The DEWALT saws have 14 stops on a stainless plate. A saw that is off by half a degree ruins miter joints. Check the saw for square before the first cut. Cut a test miter in two scrap pieces and check the joint with a square before touching the real trim.
A tall fence supports base molding standing vertically. The DWS715 supports 5-1/2 inch base, and the DWS713 4-1/4. A short fence makes tall trim lean and cut crooked.
Cordless saws like the DCS714B avoid extension cords. They need large packs for long sessions. Corded saws run indefinitely. Choose cordless only if you own the platform.

specDecoder.meaning: Positive stops are notches that click the saw to common angles. More stops speed work.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT saws list 14 stops, and others do not state their count.

specDecoder.meaning: RPM is blade speed with no load. Higher speed cuts cleaner in wood.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SKIL MS6305's 4,800 RPM is a no-load figure.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps measure motor current. A 15 amp saw has more headroom than a 10 amp saw.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SKIL 7-1/4 inch saw's 10 amps limits it on thick hardwood.

specDecoder.meaning: This is the widest board the saw can cut in one pass. It depends on blade size and slide.
specDecoder.watchFor: A listing may quote capacity at 0 degrees, but it drops at 45 degrees.

specDecoder.meaning: A shadow line projects the blade's edge, and a laser projects a dot. The shadow line shows the true kerf.

cards.label: Sliding head
cards.text: Extends crosscut width for wide boards, with some rail play. The SKIL MS6305 and Evolution R185SMS+ fall here.

cards.label: Fixed head
cards.text: Stiffer and more accurate, but limited in width. The DEWALT DWS713, DWS715 and DCS714B fall here.

howToChoose.note: Choose a slide for wide boards and a fixed head for trim and accuracy.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Baseboard needs accurate miters, a tall fence and a fine blade. Support long boards at both ends.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DEWALT DWS713 and DWS715 are the best fits. The SKIL MS6305 suits wide boards.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut trim daily or need a stand and dust collection. The DEWALT DWS715 shows where jobsite saws begin.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut occasionally. The SKIL 7-1/4 inch saw covers small projects.

maintenance.why: A fence that is off ruins miters. Use a square against the blade.

maintenance.task: Clean the detent plate and pivot
maintenance.why: Dust blocks the stops. Clean stops keep angles accurate.
A dull blade strains the motor. Fresh blades cut cleaner.

maintenance.task: Wipe and lubricate the slide rails
maintenance.why: Dust makes rails stiff. Light lubrication keeps them smooth.
Clogged ports reduce collection. Clear them with a rod.

faq.q: Should I buy a sliding or fixed saw?
faq.a: A slide cuts wider boards, and a fixed head is stiffer. Trim carpenters often choose fixed. Shelving builders choose a slide.
It buys a 10 or 12 inch saw with good stops. Listing prices move, so check the live cost. Expect basic dust collection at this level, so plan on a shop vacuum.

faq.q: How long do miter saws last?
faq.a: With care, many years. Detent plates and bearings wear first.
A larger blade cuts thicker stock. But it costs more and weighs more.
They guide, but align them. A shadow line is better. Always trust a pencil line and a test cut over any projected guide.
A stable bench or stand helps. The SKIL 7-1/4 inch saw sells its stand separately.
